s: Lakehouse → Get data → Upload files; then right-click each file → Load to Tables → New table.
SQL analytics endpoint → New SQL query → paste the sql-query-0 answer (table names lower-case as loaded).
UPDATE returns an error: the endpoint is read-only. Writes go through Spark, Dataflow Gen2, pipelines, or a Warehouse.
fab-onelake-0.check: Seven tables; Q1 2026 total {{q1_2026_gross|money0}} as in the SQL track; UPDATE not allowed.

s: Warehouse for gold: matches T-SQL skills, transactional loads (stored procedures), and its tables are Delta in OneLake so Direct Lake reads them directly.
Keep bronze/silver in a lakehouse (files, Dataflow Gen2) or mirror sources directly.
Views: OK for SQL users; for the semantic model, materialise them as tables (Direct Lake on OneLake can't use non-materialised views; Direct Lake on SQL falls back to DirectQuery for them).
fab-onelake-1.check: Warehouse gold, materialised tables for the model.

s: In Finance's lakehouse: New shortcut → Microsoft OneLake → pick the sales lakehouse table.
Ownership and changes stay with the sales data team; Finance reads the same data.
Access: Finance users need permission on the target data too; plan workspace/item permissions or OneLake security accordingly.
fab-onelake-2.check: One copy, two consumers, clear owner.
